speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent. Can you tell me how long you have had this wound on your right lower leg and if you have a history of diabetes or vascular disease?

speaker: Patient
text: 57-year-old male. The patient reports a large wound on his right lower leg that has been present for 6 months. He mentions that his legs have been chronically swollen for over 10 years and that his mother and brother had similar leg problems. He had a documented deep vein thrombosis (DVT) in the affected leg 5 years ago but has no other significant past medical history.

speaker: Doctor
text: Does the wound have a shallow, irregular base with granulation tissue, and is the surrounding skin hyperpigmented or indurated? I would also like to assess for venous stasis changes such as lipodermatosclerosis or varicose veins. REQUEST TEST: Ankle-Brachial_Index

speaker: Doctor
text: Given the history of DVT and chronic swelling, I suspect post-thrombotic syndrome despite the normal ABI. I will request imaging to evaluate the wound and venous status. REQUEST IMAGES

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Large wound on the right lower leg. I also have Chronic leg swelling, Family history of similar leg problems.

speaker: Doctor
text: Does the wound exude serous or bloody fluid, and is the surrounding skin warm and tender to the touch? I also need to know if you have any pain that worsens with elevation or improves with dependency.

speaker: Patient
text: Past medical history: Deep vein thrombosis in the right leg 5 years prior. No other significant medical history. Social history: Non-smoker, drinks alcohol socially. Works as an accountant.

speaker: Doctor
text: Does the wound bed appear pink or red with granulation tissue, and is there any purulent discharge or foul odor? I also need to know if you experience aching or heaviness in the leg that improves with elevation.

speaker: Patient
text: Denies fever, recent injuries, heart disease, or diabetes.

speaker: Doctor
text: Based on the history of DVT, chronic swelling, and venous stasis signs, this presents as a classic venous leg ulcer. DIAGNOSIS READY: Venous Leg Ulcer
